header.title: What’s new
header.sub: New seasons, engines, baselines and page changes, newest first. Follow them in a feed reader at [/feed.xml](/feed.xml).

season.closedBody: {versions} versions entered and {matches} matches played. The standings are final.

entries.title: Discord and GitHub, from every page
entries.body: The bar links our Discord server and our GitHub organisation. An error, a refused submission and a rejected version now say where to ask, and so do Get started, the FAQ and the book. Bring the version’s id and its reason.

entries.title: Admission's speed limit is the turn, and a slow model is told so
entries.body: Admission times five inferences on zero-filled inputs at your manifest's probe_dims. Their median had to fit 250 ms; it now has to fit the game's turn, 1,000 ms for Ants, the same limit play holds you to. A model over it on every attempt is rejected PROBE_TOO_SLOW, with the measured median as its inference time, where it used to expire TIMED_OUT, a reason that said the fault was ours. tinybrains check now runs the same probe and fails when the median is over the turn.

entries.title: tinybrains checks an adapter on the node's own engine
entries.body: tinybrains check and adapt now evaluate an adapter the way the node does. An object with more than one key is a template, a $-escaped key such as {"$shape": [6, 7]} is data, and try, throw and the date operators work. A key that names no operator is data on both, and tinybrains now warns about each one, because it is usually a misspelt operator the node would read as data without a word. Orion's own operators, join and the base64, hex and url codecs, run only on the node, so tinybrains refuses an adapter that calls one. Upgrade with brew upgrade tiny-brains/cli/tinybrains.

entries.title: A failed match says what went wrong, and blames no seat
entries.body: A match fails when the runner playing it goes quiet three times, or when no runner can load every model in time. Both failures are ours, so the match page no longer says a seat faulted: it says which of the two happened. Your model's own mistakes during play still count as strikes.

entries.title: A trial the platform could not run no longer counts against you
entries.body: If no runner loads a new version in time, we skip its trial, and that no longer costs you one of your three trial attempts or ends in UNPLAYABLE. Runners now get time to catch up with a new version before we give up on a match, and they play trials before ranked matches. If we still cannot load a version after three tries, we reject it as RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE. The fault is ours, so submit the same files again. A new season also shows on the site within a minute of opening.

entries.title: A notifications bell, one row for any match, and a site you can find your way round
entries.body: When you sign in, a bell in the header counts the news about your models since you last looked: admissions, rejections, passed trials, first places, strikes and season closings. New items arrive as they happen. You pick the kinds on your account page, and you can let this browser show them while the tab is in the background. Each match row now has one layout for any seat count: when and where, then up to four players in finishing order with their scores. The header holds the game and season, breadcrumbs take you up a level, your models are at /me, and your account and sessions at /me/account.

entries.title: The leaderboard and the matches, without the reading
entries.body: Both pages now open on their rows. A small meter shows the weight class, with one bar filled for nano and five for large. Icons mark a baseline, a provisional rating and a match still counting; hover one to see its name. A match row shows the score, name 0 – 3 name, with no sentence under it, and the match page shows the board and one row per seat. The size-against-rating plot is a second view of the ladder, one click from its table.

entries.title: One manifest instead of an adapter, and you upload the files
entries.body: You now submit model.onnx and manifest.json. The manifest declares what your graph takes and returns, with one adapter expression per input. A dimension may be a name, so one entry plays each board size a season runs. You no longer write the output side: the referee reads your policy head, because the channel order is a rule of the game. We now measure size as the two files’ bytes, so no way of packing the weights can understate it, and we moved each class cap to match. The platform stores none of your bytes, so a submission answers with two one-shot upload URLs, and you PUT the files to them.

entries.title: A starter you can submit unchanged
entries.body: Tiny-Brains/ants-starter holds a trained nano entry, its generated manifest, and train.py, which retrains it in one command on the baselines’ recipe. The entry scores 85.8% agreement with the teacher we distilled the baselines from. Clone it and make it yours; step 1 of Get started is that clone.

entries.title: The site says what a match came to, and draws the ladder
entries.body: Match rows and pages say what happened in words. The leaderboard plots rating against size over the class bands, names the leader of each class, and shows a sparkline of each row’s last dozen ratings. /start walks through one turn end to end, and each command on it runs. You can link to any moment in a match.

entries.title: Three trained baselines take the ladder
entries.body: We distilled nano-bc (2,930 parameters, 5.9 KiB) and micro-bc (24,001 parameters, 44.6 KiB) from one scripted teacher over 250,000 seat-turns. micro-percell is the control, with the same capacity and no receptive field. They replace untrained fixtures that held each ant still, so a trial now puts your version against an opponent that moves.

entries.title: The engine the ladder plays is one artifact
entries.body: We moved the Ants cartridge to digest 0807b641… as a patch. The ladder, the loader and the browser’s viewer take it from one image, so the component that referees a match is the one that re-simulates it.
